root_cause_label: Incorrect Weight Parsing and Tokenization Logic
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent assumed the TensorFlow .ckpt file was a raw binary float dump and that vocab.bpe was a simple newline-separated token list, leading to fundamentally wrong weight loading and tokenization that produced repetitive garbage output despite surface-level debugging.
t_err_evidence: implementation will make necessary assumptions about the format of the input model and vocabulary files (`.ckpt` as a raw float dump, `.bpe` as a simple token list)
t_commit_evidence: In Step 4, the agent types the full C implementation into the file using `cat > gpt2.c`, hard-coding the wrong weight layout (mmap of raw floats with a specific n_params=124439808 offset scheme) and a naive greedy string-matching tokenizer instead of BPE merge-based tokenization; all subsequent steps only patch surface crashes while the fundamental wrong architecture is locked in.
t_surface_evidence: ./a.out gpt2-124M.ckpt vocab.bpe "[input string here]" (followed by blank lines, no completion produced)
trigger_explanation: Before writing any code the agent explicitly decided to treat the TensorFlow checkpoint as a raw float array and the BPE vocabulary as a simple newline-delimited list, neither of which is correct. TensorFlow .ckpt files have structured binary headers/metadata, and GPT-2 BPE requires a merge-based tokenization algorithm. Every subsequent version of the code is built on this same wrong foundation.
